derivation: Distinct occupied inputs have input factorial one. In the output creation expansion, identical output rows produce the denominator t! in both the squared permanent and the distinguishable assignment sum. For a repeated two-photon output i=i this gives p_b=2 q_i1 q_i2 and p_d=q_i1 q_i2, agreeing with normalization and the HOM convention.

For arbitrary k, the number of ordered output lists for t is k!/t!. Multiplying the interference triangle bound by this multiplicity converts sum_t F(y(t))/t! to (1/k!) sum_y F(y). Summing each output position gives B_sigma(j),tau(j); each relative permutation occurs k! times. Hence 2 TV <= per B - 1, with no postselection and no missing output factorial.

Two annihilations give E_b[t_i(t_i-1)]=4 sum_(a<b) q_ia q_ib. Therefore M=sum_i(a_i^2-sum_a q_ia^2)=E_b sum_i binom(t_i,2), while the distinguishable moment is M/2. The indicator-to-moment comparison uses 1 <= sum_i binom(t_i,2) <= binom(k,2) on collisional outputs.

A=B-I is real symmetric, entrywise nonnegative and zero-diagonal. Directed simple cycles are counted up to rotation; a length-two cycle is counted once. In exp(sum C_l z^l), every collection of distinct disjoint cycles has coefficient one; all overlapping/repeated collections add nonnegative coefficients. tr(A^l)/l contains every simple cycle with its correct weight and adds nonnegative closed walks.

For l>=2, tr(A^l)>=0 follows from closed walks, including odd l. Real symmetry and monotonicity of finite vector p-norms give tr(A^l)<=sum |lambda_j|^l <= ||A||_F^l. Thus every coefficient through degree k is bounded by (!r/r!) sigma^r. Evaluating only the finite polynomial requires no sigma<1; using the infinite envelope does.

For the dominant partition, C_ga^2=sum_(i in S_g) q_ia, so every column has norm one and ||off C||_F^2=delta. Groupwise Cauchy-Schwarz gives B_ab <= (C^T C)_ab with equal diagonals. With C=D+E, ||D||op<=1, ||E||_F=sqrt(delta), ||E^T E||_F<=||E||_F^2, yielding sigma<=2 sqrt(delta)+delta even if a dominant group is empty or rows tie.

Writing d_i=a_i-max_a q_ia gives M>=sum a_i d_i>=c delta. Bounding the off-maximum squared masses by d_i^2 gives M>=2c delta-2 sum d_i^2>=2delta(c-delta). Under M<c^2/2 the independent coarse inequality forces delta<c/2; this selects the increasing branch and justifies d_c(M), rather than inverting a quadratic without branch control.

f is increasing because f′(s)=s exp(-s)/(2(1-s)^2)>=0. Its expansion f(s)=s^2/4+O(s^3), together with rho(x)=2sqrt(x)+x and fixed c, gives Phi(d_c(M))=M/(2c)+O(M^(3/2)). The cap and rho>=1 branch remain valid trivial bounds.

derivation: The two rotated occupied columns are orthonormal. All four intensities are 1/2, leakage is 2 sin^2(theta), and M=2 cos^2(theta) sin^2(theta). The three group-total probabilities are (2u,1-4u,2u) for bosons and (u,1-2u,u) for distinguishable particles. Their conditional splitting laws coincide in each group sector, so full-output TV=2u=M. This proves the stated leading sharp coefficient at c=1/2, not sharpness at every floor c.

For the flat +/- pair on even L, diagonal output probability differences sum to 1/L and same-sign distinct output differences sum to (L-2)/(2L); the positive part totals 1/2. Opposite-sign events supply the negative part 1/2. Bosonic collision probability is 2/L. Adding deterministic photons on disjoint spectator modes tensors both laws with the same point mass and preserves TV. Taking L=k+2 and k-2 spectators gives m=2k and floor 2/(k+2), as claimed.

The spectator family is physical because its occupied columns are orthonormal and can be completed to a unitary. It refutes a collision-only independent-particle certificate at balanced average density; it establishes no sampling hardness.

Haar-averaging a fixed l-photon bosonic density matrix commutes with all passive mode transformations. Diagonal mode phases force the averaged operator to be diagonal in the occupation basis; commutation with mode-mixing generators a_i^dagger a_j equates adjacent occupation diagonal entries, since the composition graph is connected. Unit trace then gives uniform weight 1/binom(m+l-1,l). There are binom(m,k) binom(l-1,k-1) compositions with exactly k occupied modes. This independently reconstructs h(l); it is not an independent authentication of the cited source/version.

Uniform independent loss produces Bin(N,eta) survivors and commutes through a passive interferometer. Conditioning on any surviving distinct-input subset, the same Haar average applies. Thus S_N=E h(L), with vacuum and all failures counted.

The exact h ratio minus one has numerator k(m-2-l); birth at l=k-1 is positive, the difference at m-2 is zero and the one at m-1 negative. Coupling one Bernoulli survivor gives S_(N+1)-S_N=eta E Delta h(Bin(N,eta)). This is strictly positive for N<=m-2 and has one crossing for N=m-1. At eta=1 the maximum h(m-2)=h(m-1) gives exactly the stated endpoint tie.

Binomial size bias gives b_N=eta E g(Bin(N-1,eta)+1); one additional Bernoulli trial gives the eta^2 adjacent-difference identity. The g-ratio numerator is [m(m-2)-(m+2)l]/2, with zero m-4+8/(m+2) strictly between m-4 and m-3 for m>=8. This yields the four possible source sizes and the endpoint optimum m-3.

For the sign-change lemma, division by t^a leaves positive terms with negative exponents and negative terms with nonnegative exponents, making a strictly decreasing function from positive infinity to a negative limit. For successive binomial orders, the mass likelihood ratio (1-eta)(n+1)/(n+1-r) is strictly increasing in r; centering it at the coefficient sign boundary makes the new expectation negative at the old root. Thus tau_(m-1)<tau_(m-2)<tau_(m-3). Ordered adjacent differences exclude nonadjacent global ties.

derivation: With N=m-s and T the number lost, l=m-s-T. Expanding the exact ratios on l>=3m/4 gives Delta h/h=(s+T-2)/(2m)+O((1+s+T)^2/m^2) and Delta g/g=(s+T-4)/(2m)+O((1+s+T)^2/m^2). After size bias, T is Bin(m-s-1,lambda/m), so l remains m-s-T: there is no missing shift by one.

Peak-relative values differ from one by O((1+s+T)^2/m), and are bounded. All fixed moments and a positive exponential moment of T are uniformly bounded at fixed lambda. Multiplying the ratio errors by peak-relative errors therefore contributes O(m^-2) in expectation. Markov applied to exp(T) gives an exponentially small tail beyond m/4-s; functions and adjacent differences divided by their peaks are bounded there. Division by the mean preserves the stated expansion.

The explicit index dictionary is m(1-a_m)->1, m(1-tau_(m-3))->1, m(1-tau_(m-2))->2, and m(1-tau_(m-1))->3. The per-photon losses 1,2,3 are in the order of the optimum transitions m-3 to m-2 to m-1 to m as eta decreases, rather than ascending eta-root order. Fixed-lambda sign bracketing and unique crossings suffice to establish these limits.
The argument is pointwise in fixed s and lambda and is not a fixed-transmission or uniform growing-lambda assertion. The manuscript expressly maintains this distinction.

The internal-state overlap factor is S_(tau(j),sigma(j)): it follows by taking the internal norm of the amplitude vector sum_sigma product_j V_(y_j,sigma(j)) tensor_j phi_(sigma(j)). This gives the stated conjugation convention and the p_b and p_d endpoints.

For two photons, only identity and transposition interference occur, so x=|S_12|^2 gives p_x=x p_b+(1-x)p_d. With uniform loss the zero- and one-photon detected sectors have the same spatial distribution for every x. Hence detected full-space TV to x=0 is eta^2 x M0.

For the sharp family, the two same-group sectors have probabilities (1+x)u each. Half of each sector bunches and half gives the corresponding valid optimum path string. Therefore P_collision=P_success_path=eta^2(1+x)u=eta^2(1+x)M0/2. This uses all occupations and does not condition on detection.

The rotation parametrization theta=2 arctan(r) agrees with BS.Rx(4 arctan(r)), whose convention uses a half angle. Routing and group splitters implement the sharp family up to output phases and input-column phases; fixed distinct-input Fock probabilities are invariant under those phases. The claim is about displayed occupation laws, not exact phase-identical matrices.

For k>=3, transposition overlap factors and longer-cycle products need not share a single mixture coefficient. The global-mixture warning is consistent with the stated product pure internal-state model.

checks.arithmetic: Python fractions.Fraction, math.comb; no random sampling, external packages or network
algorithm: Compute h(m,l)=comb(m,m/2)*comb(l-1,m/2-1)/comb(m+l-1,l) as a Fraction, zero below m/2. Sum the exact binomial mixture for every N in [m/2,m]. Enumerate all maximizing N for S_N and S_N/N.
For m=8,10,12 and l=m/2,...,m-1, compare h(m,l+1)/h(m,l) exactly to l(l+1)/((l-m/2+1)(m+l)).

For r=1/10 use c=(1-r^2)/(1+r^2), s=2r/(1+r^2), A=((c,-s),(c,-s),(s,c),(s,c)) so V=A/sqrt(2). Enumerate all ten ordered-index pairs i<=j. Compute p_b=(A_i0*A_j1+A_i1*A_j0)^2/(8 if i=j else 4) and p_d=(A_i0^2*A_j1^2+A_i1^2*A_j0^2)/(8 if i=j else 4). Verify normalization, TV=M, collision mass=M and optimal-path mass=M.

For each of the nine x/eta combinations, interpolate p_x=x p_b+(1-x)p_d and verify eta^2 TV(p_x,p_d)=eta^2 x M and both collision/path masses eta^2(1+x)M/2. Equality of lower loss sectors was derived analytically in MA-C007, not inferred from a zero-shot experiment.

checked_comparisons: Abstract and discussion explicitly require a floor on every positive row; they distinguish expected collision pairs from collision probability, fixed-c upper envelopes from circuitwise asymptotic equivalence, and average density from a row floor.
The sharp coefficient is claimed only at c=1/2. The spectator family is claimed as an obstruction to a specific independent-particle approximation, not as computational hardness.
Same-circuit absolute TV control is explicitly separated from rare-event ratios, retrained-model comparisons, and graph-optimization benefit.

The loss theorem is explicitly Haar-averaged threshold feasibility, with different resource normalizations and no graph-quality enrichment. The text distinguishes refreshed-Haar N/E[p] from the fixed-U expectation E[N/p].

The optimization grid arithmetic is internally consistent: 3*6*2*3*7=756 runs, 36 runs per method/size, and 120*256+4096=34816 ideal attempts. The displayed bosonic means are lower than the distinguishable means at all sizes. Descriptive intervals, duplicate graph seeds, oracle-assisted historical runs and unknown within-batch first-hit order are disclosed.

The lower-priority mean-objective and pinched-state results are not presented as full samplers or proofs of the open measured TV<=delta bound. Static ObliQ reproduction is not presented as full original training/decoding reproduction.
